title: Why leave your home
hookLine: the yogis catch the traveler who praises staying, and ask why he left home

cards: Fair point, the yogis might say. You tell us to stay in the stream, work, keep a home. So what are you doing up here?

The man praising the household life is standing on a mountain, far from his own household, dressed for the road. In the Sidh Gosht they put it to him directly. Why did you leave your home and become a wanderer, an udasi?
Why take on this way of dressing? What are you trading in, and how will you carry anyone across? It's the sharpest question yet, because it's about him.

teach.b: Nanak's answer, in paraphrase: searching for the Gurmukhs, I became a wanderer. I took on this way of dressing for the sake of a glimpse of the One. I'm a trader in the merchandise of truth.
And through the Guru, a person crosses over and carries others across. Piece by piece. First, he went looking for people: Gurmukhs, those whose faces are turned toward the Guru.
Not a place, not a secret, not a technique; people who live facing the good. In his telling, he didn't go out to get away from the world. He went out to find the best of it.

teach.h: THE ROAD CLOTHES SERVE THE LONGING.
teach.b: He doesn't claim his road clothes make him holy. They serve the looking, the longing for a glimpse; the outfit is for the journey, not the point of it. Third, the trade.
A trader goes from town to town, buying here, selling there. Nanak takes that picture for himself. What he carries is truth, and the deal is that it gets passed on.

So the traveling doesn't contradict the duck. The duck was never told to sit still; it swims. Tradition says Nanak's journeys ended at Kartarpur, where he settled, farmed and kept a household, with people coming to him.

teach.h: THE ROAD SEEKS; HOME LIVES IT.
teach.b: The road was for seeking and sharing; home was where it was lived.
And the question doesn't offend him. They catch him in what looks like a contradiction, and he simply tells them why.

how: Sikhs remember Guru Nanak's long journeys as the udasis, and read this exchange in the Sidh Gosht as his own account of why he traveled: to seek the Gurmukhs and share the Name.

games.q: what does “why leave your home” mean?
o: a hymn of homesickness from Nanak's long travels
a map of the roads Nanak walked on his journeys
the yogis' question, answered: he left to seek the Gurmukhs

games.q: the question and the answer — tap the pairs.
p: a wanderer who has left home
people whose faces turn to the Guru
for the sake of a glimpse

s: Nanak says he left home to escape the world
he says he went searching for the Gurmukhs, to find the best of it.
Nanak calls himself a trader in truth
in his answer he is a merchant whose merchandise is truth.
Nanak claims his road clothes make him holy
he says he took them on for the sake of a glimpse of the One.

games.q: you've told the yogis to live in the world like a duck in the stream. they ask why you're on the road, far from home. what does Nanak answer?
o: that the world is too dirty to stay in.
that he went searching for the Gurmukhs and trades in truth.
that the yogis were right all along.
games.why: he says he became a wanderer to search for the Gurmukhs, and that what he carries is the merchandise of truth.

practice: Bring to mind someone you've met who lives facing the good, kind without fuss, honest when it costs something, and let their face come clearly.

What's one good thing you picked up from them, a habit, a sentence, a way of treating people? Hold it for a few breaths, the way a trader holds something worth carrying, and if you pray, give thanks for the person you pictured.

wordCard.voice: Why leave your home. The yogis' question to the traveler, and Nanak's answer: searching for the Gurmukhs, and trading in truth. Today's word.

orig.note: udasi: one who has left home and wanders; the yogis' word for what Nanak seemed to have become.

carryVoice: Your line: seeking the good. A trader in truth carries it on. Thanks for sitting with me.

sources.ref: Guru Granth Sahib, Ramkali, Mahala 1, Sidh Gosht, pauris 17–18, Ang 939 (why did you leave home; searching for the Gurmukhs; trader in truth)
Vaaran Bhai Gurdas, Var 1 (Guru Nanak settles at Kartarpur)
